newsitem.title: UK: June Brent in mild downward slant but off lows.
newsitem.headline: June Brent in mild downward slant but off lows.

text.p: IPE June Brent maintained a slightly downward slant on Wednesday after a short-lived dip following losses on NYMEX, traders said.

June Brent was trading two cents down at $18.59 a barrel by 1454 GMT, shortly after hitting the day's low of $18.48. May gas oil was $1.50 a tonne higher at $170.25, in line with its earlier levels, mildly supported by weekly U.S. date on gasoline stocks slipping.
"You have to watch the products' expiry today in the States. A lot of people are expecting a squeeze on the May heating oil (on NYMEX)," a broker said.
The May WTI contract on NYMEX, which expires at the end of Wednesday's trading, was 11 cents down at $20.31 a barrel while May heating oil was 0.31 cents a gallon down at 58.50 cents.
Brokers said they saw resistance at $18.64 and $18.70 for June Brent, with support at $18.30 and major support at the $18.20 level.

The American Petroleum Institute (API) said in its weekly data released late on Tuesday that middle distillate stocks fell by 1.4 million barrels last week, gasoline stocks fell a modest 408,000 barrels, while crude stocks rose by 1.87 million barrels.
